scenes.heading: Stem cells
scenes.sub: One cell became hundreds of cell types. How?
scenes.say: You began as a single cell. Now your body has hundreds of kinds of cells, from nerve cells to red blood cells. Stem cells made that possible, and they keep repairing you for life.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: A footy academy keeps some juniors and promotes others
scenes.breaks: Senior players can go back and coach. Most specialised cells can't become stem cells again on their own.
scenes.say: Think of a footy club's junior academy. It keeps some players back to train next year, and promotes others to fixed positions in the seniors. Stem cells do both. Self-renewal makes more stem cells. Differentiation makes specialised cells. But most specialised cells can't go back to being stem cells on their own.

scenes.heading: Differentiation
points: Almost every cell has the same DNA
Specialised cells usually can't change type
scenes.say: Almost every cell in your body has the same DNA. So how do they become different? They express, or switch on, different genes. Same cookbook, different recipes. Signals from the cell's surroundings help decide which genes are switched on.

scenes.heading: Potency rolls downhill
scenes.say: Potency is how many cell types a stem cell can become. Totipotent cells, like the zygote, can make every type, including the placenta. Pluripotent cells, from the inner cell mass, make any body cell. Multipotent cells, like blood stem cells, make one family. Unipotent cells make just one type.

scenes.heading: Embryonic vs iPS cells

left.title: Embryonic stem cells
points: From a blastocyst's inner cell mass

scenes.say: Embryonic stem cells are pluripotent, but collecting them destroys an embryo, and donor cells risk rejection. Induced pluripotent stem cells, or iPS cells, are adult cells rewound in the lab. No embryo is needed, and they match the patient. But reprogramming can cause genetic changes and tumours.

scenes.heading: Classify the potency
scenes.question: A bone marrow cell can form red blood cells, white blood cells and platelets, but not nerve or muscle cells. What is its potency?
lines: Makes more than one type: not unipotent
All are blood cells: one family
Can't make nerve cells: not pluripotent
scenes.say: A bone marrow cell can make red blood cells, white blood cells and platelets, but not nerve or muscle cells. It makes more than one type, so it's not unipotent. But they're all one family, blood cells. So it's multipotent.

points: Differentiation = switching genes on and off
scenes.say: Quick recap. Stem cells self-renew and differentiate. Differentiation means switching different genes on and off. Potency narrows from toti, to pluri, to multi, to uni. Bone marrow transplants are an established treatment, and many others are still being researched. Now try the practice questions!
